# SurveyBeat

Cloudflare-only Effect app. One Durable Object per Organization is the system of record; D1 holds only the global index and auth/email bookkeeping, never survey content. Two Workers serve the app/API (`MainWorker`) and the answer page's submission path (`SubmissionWorker`).

Read `SPEC.md` (authoritative spec), `GLOSSARY.md` (domain vocabulary), and `docs/adr/` (binding decisions) before changing behavior. `docs/infra.md` covers stages, WorkOS sign-in, email, and observability.

## Ground rules

- Use glossary terms exactly: Pulse (not Survey), Person (not User), Round (not instance), Submission (not Response). Do not drift to the "avoid" synonyms.
- If a change contradicts an ADR, say so and add a new ADR under `docs/adr/`; never silently override one.
- Issues and specs live in GitHub issues (`gh`); conventions are in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`. Commit subjects name the release slice, e.g. `R1 03: ...`.
- Privacy invariants are release blockers (SPEC §7): anonymous Submissions store no Person and no time (ADR 0005), comments are redacted at store time (ADR 0009), and every shown aggregate obeys the minimum group size (ADR 0004).

## Commands (from the repo root)

Node 24 (`.node-version`) and pnpm 12.18.0 are pinned.

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm typecheck          # tsc -b with project references
pnpm typecheck:effect   # @effect/tsgo diagnostics; CI runs this first
pnpm lint               # oxlint --type-aware
pnpm format             # oxfmt; CI runs format:check
pnpm test               # Vitest "unit" project only
pnpm test:privacy       # Vitest "privacy" project only; NOT part of pnpm test
pnpm test <path>        # one file, e.g. pnpm test packages/domain/src/people/SignIn.test.ts
pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web build
```

CI runs `typecheck:effect`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `lint`, `test`, then the web build; the privacy suite is a separate required job. There is no root `dev` script: `pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web dev` serves the UI only, and the app calls the API at `window.location.origin`. Exercise sign-in and end-to-end flows on a deployed stage.

## Layout and boundaries

- `packages/domain` — Effect schemas and services by concept (`people/`, `email/`); depends only on `effect`.
- `packages/api` — the `HttpApi` declaration shared by the Worker and the typed web client; depends on `domain`.
- `packages/cloudflare` — all Cloudflare adapters plus the `MainWorker` and `SubmissionWorker` entries; the only package that touches the Alchemy runtime.
- `apps/web` — one Vite project with two entries: the React app (`index.html`) and the plain-TypeScript answer page (`answer.html`).
- `packages/emails` — React Email templates and rendering. `packages/testing` — privacy harness. `infra` — Alchemy stack, scripts, Playwright e2e, privacy sweep. `tools/oxlint-plugin-surveybeat` — local lint rules.

## Toolchain traps

- Effect is 4.1.2, not 3.x. Import from `effect/Effect`, `effect/Schema`, `effect/http-api`, `effect/http/...`; there is no `@effect/platform` v3-style API here. Copy the import style from neighboring files.
- TypeScript 7 (native compiler) with `tsc -b`. A new package needs its own `tsconfig.json` and an entry in the root `tsconfig.json` references.
- Stricter than defaults: `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax` (use `import type`), and relative imports carry explicit `.ts`/`.tsx` extensions.
- Lint bans `any` and type assertions (`as Foo`) outside `*.test.ts` (`consistent-type-assertions: never`). Decode with Effect Schema or use typed helpers instead.
- All user-facing text comes from `apps/web/src/messages/catalog.ts` or `packages/emails/src/messages/catalog.ts`; `no-literal-ui-text` fails otherwise. HTML shells must hold no visible text and an empty `<title>` (asserted in `messages.test.ts`). Plurals use `<base>.one`/`.other`.
- The lint plugin enforces the boundaries: `domain`/`api` may not import `cloudflare:*` or Alchemy, and `apps/web/src/answer/**` may not import React, Base UI, or the HttpApi client.
- Keep the answer entry plain TypeScript within its budget (JS ≤ 10 KB gzip critical path, CSS ≤ 2 KB inline, HTML ≤ 8 KB); no framework, per ADR 0008.

## Tests

- Tests are colocated `*.test.ts`. A privacy test must be named `*.privacy.test.ts` or CI never runs it.
- Use `@effect/vitest` (`it.effect` for Effect programs).
- Adapter tests use `@alchemy.run/test`'s `Test.make({ dev: true })` against local workerd and are slow (deploy timeouts up to 240 s); run the single file you need.
- A new API endpoint must be classified in `packages/api/src/PrivacyRegistry.ts` or the package will not typecheck; `registry.privacy.test.ts` checks the runtime declaration too.
- End-to-end tests run only against a deployed stage: `E2E_BASE_URL=https://pr-<n>.app.surveybeat.app pnpm test:e2e` (install Chromium once with `pnpm --filter @surveybeat/infra exec playwright install chromium`).

## Infra

- Every Cloudflare resource is declared in `infra/alchemy.run.ts`; no dashboard edits, no wrangler config.
- Run Alchemy from the repo root: the Organization DO migrations path (`packages/cloudflare/migrations`) is relative to the working directory. Build the web app first; the Main Worker serves `apps/web/dist`.
- `pnpm infra:deploy --stage dev-<name>` needs `WORKOS_API_KEY`, `WORKOS_CLIENT_ID`, and `ORG_CREATION_ALLOWLIST` in the environment.
- Non-production stages never send real email; sends are recorded in D1's `captured_email`. Only `production` sends.
- The Submission Worker must keep every observability channel off. `pnpm check:observability --stage <stage>` reads the deployed settings back; the canary sweep proves no logs are kept. Stage scripts need `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`.
- New SQL migrations: numbered files in `packages/cloudflare/migrations` (Durable Object) or `packages/cloudflare/d1-migrations` (D1).

- [Cloudflare cf CLI](cloudflare-cf-cli.md) — authenticated cf CLI for SurveyBeat's Cloudflare account; discover commands with cf cli search
- [Wayfinder: always push and merge](wayfinder-always-push-merge.md) — push and squash-merge each resolved ticket's branch without asking

Slice 7 of [Release 1: implementation](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/34).

## Goal
Rounds run themselves: open per time zone, close once, compute, share, and create the next one, even if any job runs twice.

## Acceptance criteria
- A schedule table plus one alarm set to the earliest due job. Each job is an idempotent DO method that runs in the same transaction as its state change.
- States: Scheduled → Open → Closed → Ready → Shared (Ready moves straight to Shared in R1), plus Cancelled.
- Open happens at the first member's local send. Eligible members are frozen then. **One close instant: the latest member's send time plus the window.**
- The next Round is always Scheduled. It is created with the Pulse and again at each open, keyed by Pulse and planned open date.
- Lead controls:
  - skip any of the next 8 weeks (skipping the Scheduled week cancels it);
  - pause cancels the Scheduled Round, and an Open Round runs to its end;
  - close early (uninvited members are never invited);
  - cancelling an Open Round deletes its Submissions and Participation records.
- A Scheduled Round picks up Pulse changes. An Open Round never changes.
- IANA time zones. Local times are converted to UTC when scheduled. In a daylight-saving gap the time moves forward; in an overlap the first occurrence wins.
- The daily Cron repairs missing alarms.
- The close job enqueues result computation. The compute itself is slice 11, so use a stub here.

## Tests
Run every job twice and check nothing changes the second time. A Round spanning UTC−8 and UTC+9. A daylight-saving transition. Skip, pause, close, and cancel.

Slice 8 of [Release 1: implementation](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/34).

## Goal
Each eligible member gets exactly one Invitation email with one-tap rating links, plus reminders at their local time.

## Acceptance criteria
- One Invitation row per Round and Person, created at open, with a 128-bit base64url token stored only as a hash (in D1 for lookup and in the DO). The token is revoked when the member is removed or the Round is cancelled.
- The Invitation email has:
  - the Pulse name;
  - a one-line anonymity statement;
  - five text-labelled rating links `https://app.surveybeat.app/a#t=<token>&v=<n>` (the **token is in the fragment**);
  - "Open check-in";
  - up to three Actions (an empty slot until slice 13);
  - the footer: "Change when I get this", "This link is personal. Don't forward it."
- Reminders go at the member's own send time on later days of the window:
  - with one reminder, on day W−1;
  - with two, on day 1 and day W−1;
  - with W = 1, 6 hours after the send;
  - skipped if the member has answered, has opted out, or close is less than 2 hours away.
- Reminder opt-out per Person per Pulse: RFC 8058 `List-Unsubscribe` with a POST endpoint, no redirect, and DKIM-covered headers.
- The "Change when I get this" page runs on the Main Worker, with the token in the POST body. It suggests the browser's time zone and never touches answers.
- The Lead's view lists failed Invitations with their reason and a **Resend** button.

No Invitation is sent twice when the open job runs twice. Reminder schedule tests. GET and HEAD of any token link perform zero writes.

# Executor

## What Executor is

Executor is a host that runs apps: TypeScript packages that expose tools,
storage, UI, accounts and background work. Agents reach every app through the
MCP tools `skills`, `search`, `describe`, `call` and `execute`, with each app's
slug as its namespace. Credentials go only through Executor's secure connection
links, never through chat or source code. Some calls pause for user approval.

`tools.<slug>.<tool>`, and input type; `describe({ paths })` returns full
signatures. Never guess argument names.

For a few independent calls, use `call({ calls: { path, input } })`; an array

Build an app when no existing app provides the tools, data, UI or automation
the user needs. For a known service, search the catalog first:
`organization.catalog({ query: { search: "gmail", limit: "20" } })`, then
`apps.install` a match or `apps.importCustom` a remote MCP URL. With a shell,
use the `executor apps` CLI, else `execute`; read the `app-authoring` skill first.

Send feedback with the Executor app's `feedback.submit` tool when Executor gets
in your way, can't do something you need, works especially well, or the user
has feedback. Before your final reply, check whether anything is worth
reporting. Be specific; never include credentials or user data (`feedback.md`).

## Changes

The Rounds list and the Lead controls are in the web app, and the 3 failing scene tests are fixed. Everything I changed is under `apps/web/`.

- **New route:** `Rounds` at `/teams/:teamId/pulses/:pulseId/rounds`, with `roundsRouter` and `roundsHref` in `apps/web/src/app/routes.ts`.
- **Reaching it:** `apps/web/src/app/pulses.ts` shows a "Rounds" link on the Pulse editor page only when `team.yourRole === "lead"`. Org admins outside the Team, and Members, never see the link.
- **New screen:** `apps/web/src/app/rounds.ts` is the Rounds list, with these pieces:
  - Each row shows the Round date, status and dates.
  - For a Lead only, closed, ready or shared rounds also show the response rate and a "View Results" link.
  - Lead controls are skip, pause/resume, close early, cancel, and Resend on failed Invitations.
  - Close early and cancel open an `alertdialog` confirm with "Yes, continue" and "Keep Round". The API is called only after "Yes, continue".
  - An Org admin who opens the URL sees the list only. A Member gets the Forbidden problem from the list call.
- **Wiring:** `apps/web/src/app/App.ts` gets the new model fields, messages and commands. It loads the Team first, then `listRounds`, then follow-ups for Leads only. Open rounds get `getRound` (for failed Invitations), closed rounds get `getResults` (for the rate). Every command refreshes the list afterwards.
- **Messages:** new `rounds.*` keys and `pulse.rounds` in `apps/web/src/messages/catalog.ts`. I did not touch any `answer.*` keys.
- **Scene test fixes:** the two "Not enough answers to protect anonymity" assertions and "3 Submissions received so far." are updated. I added `contributors: 6` to the Dimension fixture.

## Endpoints each control calls
- **Rounds list:** `GET /api/teams/:teamId/pulses/:pulseId/rounds`
- **Failed Invitations:** `GET /api/teams/:teamId/rounds/:roundId`
- **Response rate:** `GET /api/teams/:teamId/rounds/:roundId/results`
- **Resend:** `POST /api/teams/:teamId/rounds/:roundId/invitations/:personId/resend`
- **Skip week:** `POST /api/teams/:teamId/pulses/:pulseId/skip`. It is offered per Scheduled row and through a "date YYYY-MM-DD" field for any of the next 8 weeks.
- **Pause / Resume:** `POST /api/teams/:teamId/pulses/:pulseId/pause` and `.../resume`
- **Close early:** `POST /api/teams/:teamId/rounds/:roundId/close`
- **Cancel:** `POST /api/teams/:teamId/rounds/:roundId/cancel`

## Missing from the API
- **Paused state:** `PulseDetail` and `RoundList` do not say whether a Pulse is paused. `SqlRounds` has `isPulsePaused`, but it is not exposed. I show both "Pause Pulse" and "Resume Pulse" buttons for now. A `paused` flag on the list would let the screen show only the one that applies.
- **Response rate in the list:** `RoundSummary` has no counts. I call `getResults` once per closed Round, and only for Leads. If you want this cheaper, add `submissionsCount` and `eligibleMembersCount` to `RoundSummary`.
- **Failed Invitations in the list:** they come only from `RoundDetail`, so I call `getRound` once per open Round. Resend only works on open Rounds anyway.
- **`unskipWeek`:** I did not build a UI for it.

## Validation
- `pnpm test apps/web`: 4 files, 44 tests, all passing. This includes the new Rounds scene tests and two new story tests (`App.story.test.ts`) for the Team-then-Rounds load chain, one of which checks an Org admin outside the Team triggers no detail or Results calls.
- `pnpm format` then `pnpm format:check`: clean.
- `pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web build`: succeeds.
- `pnpm typecheck`: no errors in `apps/web/src/app` or the web messages. Other errors remain in files owned by other agents: `packages/cloudflare` (including `Organization.ts`, which `apps/web` does not import), `packages/testing`, and `apps/web/src/answer/main.ts` and `vite.config.ts` for the missing `answer.anonymity` key.
- `pnpm lint`: one error, `packages/testing/src/SqliteStorage.ts:34` (`consistent-type-assertions`). It is not in my files, and I did not check whether it predates my work.

## Notes
- `pnpm format` runs on the whole repo, and other agents' files were modified at the same time, so I cannot rule out that it reformatted some of them.
- The existing mock Team detail in `App.scene.test.ts` uses `abilities:` where the schema says `may`. I left it alone and used `may` in my fixtures.
